chain.title: One company, the whole chain
chain.lede: Most of this chain is where a small brand loses money — a supplier who cannot make the quantity, a run that arrives off-spec, a shipment nobody is tracking. Brandora Union runs all six links, so no one of them is somebody else's problem.

ask.title: Not sure what to source?
ask.lede: Describe what you need in your own words. Brandora reads the request, searches the real catalogue and tells you what can actually be ordered at your quantity.
ask.grounding: It answers from the catalogue and your stored brand — never from guesswork. If nothing fits, it says so instead of suggesting something that does not exist.
ask.example.q: I need 2,000 luxury cosmetic boxes, matte black, with my logo, delivered to Abidjan.
ask.example.a: Reads the quantity, the material, the finish, the branding and the destination — then shortlists only what is recorded as orderable at 2,000, and says what is missing rather than filling it in.
network.title: Between the brand and the factory
network.lede: A founder in Abidjan and a manufacturer who can make what they need are usually two people who will never meet. Brandora Union is the connection — and the quality check, the paperwork and the shipment that have to come with it.
network.brands.note: An idea, an identity, and a quantity small enough to test.
network.makers.note: Capacity, tooling and a price that only holds at volume.

founder.p1: I built Brandora Union because I noticed a gap I couldn't ignore.
founder.p2: Across Africa, there are incredible entrepreneurs building ambitious brands and creating genuinely great products. But too often, the physical presentation of those products doesn't reflect the quality of what's inside.
founder.p3: I realized that packaging is not just packaging. It is often the first conversation a customer has with a brand. Before they taste, wear, use, or experience a product, they see it. The shape, the materials, the details, the colors — all of it creates an immediate feeling about what's inside.
founder.pull1: A beautiful, thoughtful package can make a product feel intentional, trustworthy, and worth discovering.
founder.p4: Yet for many African brands, accessing high-quality, customized packaging and reliable manufacturing partners can still be difficult, expensive, or unnecessarily complicated.
founder.p6: I created Brandora Union to make it easier for African entrepreneurs to build brands that look and feel as exceptional as the products they create — by connecting them with the right products, packaging, manufacturers, and eventually the entire infrastructure needed to bring their ideas into the physical world.
founder.p7: Africa has the ideas. Africa has the talent. I believe our brands should have the infrastructure to match.
founder.pull2: And Côte d'Ivoire is where I'm starting.

legal.privacy.title: Privacy policy
legal.privacy.intro: Brandora Union (“Brandora”, “we”) builds brands and sources the physical products behind them for small businesses, from Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire. This page describes what we collect through brandoraunion.online, why, and what you can ask us to do about it.
legal.privacy.p.collect-1: When you create an account: your name, email address and password, and — only if you choose to give them — your country and phone number.
legal.privacy.p.collect-2: When you use the brand builder: your answers to the interview questions (your business, product, audience and positioning), and the brand, identity and package that Brandora generates from them.
legal.privacy.p.collect-3: When you request a quote, place an order, or upload a logo for a manufacturer: the details you enter in that form, and the file itself.
legal.privacy.p.collect-4: If you sign in with Google, we receive the name, email address and profile photo Google shares for that purpose — nothing else from your Google account.
legal.privacy.p.use: To run your account, generate your brand, price and fulfil your orders, answer your quote requests, and reply when you contact us. We do not sell your data, and we do not use it to show you advertising.
legal.privacy.p.share-1: A small number of providers process data on our behalf, only for the purpose stated: Anthropic generates your brand strategy and identity from your interview answers; Resend delivers our transactional emails (account, orders, quotes); Paystack processes payments — Brandora never sees or stores your card details; and, if you use them, Google for sign-in and Calendly for booking a call operate under their own privacy policies for that interaction.
legal.privacy.p.share-2: We do not share your data with anyone else, and we do not run advertising or analytics trackers on this site.
legal.privacy.p.cookies: One cookie keeps you signed in — it identifies your session and nothing else, and it is not readable by any script on this page. Your language, your light-or-dark preference, and which brand you were last working on are kept in your browser's own storage, on your device, so returning to the site does not lose them.
legal.privacy.p.retention-1: We keep your data for as long as your account is active. We do not yet have a self-service way to export or delete your account — email
legal.privacy.p.retention-2: and we will handle it directly.
legal.privacy.p.rights: You can ask us what we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it, at the same address. We will act on a deletion request unless we are required to keep something — a paid order's record, for example — for accounting or legal reasons.
legal.privacy.p.children: Brandora is a business-to-business service and is not directed at children. We do not knowingly collect data from anyone under 16.
legal.privacy.p.changes: If this policy changes in a way that matters, we will update the date at the top of this page and, for a significant change, tell you by email.
legal.terms.title: Terms of service
legal.terms.intro: These are the terms for using brandoraunion.online, run by Brandora Union from Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire. Creating an account, requesting a quote, or placing an order means you accept them.
legal.terms.p.service-1: Brandora generates a brand — a name, positioning, palette and identity — from the answers you give, and helps you turn it into physical products from our catalogue. Some products carry a fixed price at a given quantity; others are marked “price on request” because the cost depends on a freight quote we have not yet obtained, and we will not show you an invented figure in its place.
legal.terms.p.service-2: There is no manufacturer marketplace on Brandora yet. Clicking a product photo to request a quote sends your request to us by email; we follow up directly rather than through an automated portal.
legal.terms.p.accounts: You are responsible for the accuracy of the information on your account and for keeping your password confidential. You must be able to enter into a binding contract to create one.
legal.terms.p.orders-1: Prices are shown in West African CFA francs (XOF) and include Brandora's sourcing and coordination margin. A quote is valid for the period stated on it; after that, prices may have changed and a new quote is needed.
legal.terms.p.orders-2: Payment is processed by Paystack. We never see or store your card details. An order is confirmed once payment is verified as received.
legal.terms.p.delivery: Delivery charges shown at checkout are Brandora's own local delivery fee, not a carrier's quote — we do not publish a delivery date until one has actually been confirmed for your order.
legal.terms.p.cancellation: Because most orders are manufactured for you rather than held in stock, cancellation terms depend on how far production has gone when you ask — contact us as soon as you know, and we will tell you exactly where things stand.
legal.terms.p.ip: The brand, name and identity Brandora generates for you are yours once your order is paid. Brandora Union retains ownership of the software, the catalogue and the site itself.
legal.terms.p.liability: We work to get pricing, availability and delivery information right, but Brandora is not liable for indirect losses arising from delays or errors outside our reasonable control, including from our suppliers or payment provider.
legal.terms.p.law: These terms are governed by the law of Côte d'Ivoire.
legal.terms.p.changes: If we change these terms in a way that matters, we will update the date at the top of this page.

pricing.title: How pricing works
pricing.lede: A formula, not an eyeballed guess. Here is exactly what makes up the price you see, and why.
pricing.formula.label: The formula
pricing.formula.text: Final price = Product cost + Shipping cost + Brandora service margin
pricing.p.product-cost: What the manufacturer charges for the product itself, from the real supplier behind every item in the catalogue — never an approximate figure.
pricing.p.shipping-cost: The estimated — or, once confirmed, real — logistics cost tied to your order: international freight, customs and local delivery, as applicable.
pricing.p.margin-1: A transparent percentage, added on top of the product cost and shipping cost together, to cover sourcing, supplier coordination, quality control, order management and running the platform. This rate is configurable rather than hardcoded — it is currently set to
pricing.p.margin-2: , within a disclosed range of 25 to 35%.
pricing.example.note: For illustration only — your real quotes are shown in West African CFA francs (XOF).
pricing.p.states-1: — calculated from the product chosen, the quantity, and an estimated supplier cost and shipping. This is what you see while browsing the catalogue.
pricing.p.states-2: — once we have spoken with the manufacturer: final supplier price, confirmed shipping, and the same Brandora margin. Manufacturing prices move with minimum quantity, material, customization, packaging, destination and shipping method — the confirmed quote accounts for all of it.
pricing.h.transparency: What we show, what we keep private
pricing.p.transparency: We are transparent about the method: your price is product cost + shipping + Brandora's service margin. The exact cost negotiated with each supplier stays in our internal system — being transparent about the formula does not mean disclosing our suppliers' confidential commercial terms.
